You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE stadium (
    Stadium_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Location TEXT,
    Name TEXT,
    Capacity INT,
    Highest INT,
    Lowest INT,
    Average INT,
    UNIQUE (Stadium_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE singer (
    Singer_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Song_Name TEXT,
    Song_release_year TEXT,
    Age INT,
    Is_male bool,
    UNIQUE (Singer_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE concert (
    concert_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    concert_Name TEXT,
    Theme TEXT,
    Stadium_ID TEXT,
    Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (concert_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Stadium_ID) REFERENCES stadium(Stadium_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE singer_in_concert (
    concert_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Singer_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    PRIMARY KEY (concert_ID, Singer_ID),
    UNIQUE (concert_ID, Singer_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Singer_ID) REFERENCES singer(Singer_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (concert_ID) REFERENCES concert(concert_ID)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

Assuming “big stadium” means stadiums with capacity above the average capacity, this query summarizes each big stadium with concert and singer counts:

```sql
SELECT
    s.Stadium_ID,
    s.Name,
    s.Location,
    s.Capacity,
    s.Highest,
    s.Lowest,
    s.Average AS Average_Attendance,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.concert_ID) AS Concert_Count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT sic.Singer_ID) AS Singer_Count
FROM stadium AS s
LEFT JOIN concert AS c
    ON c.Stadium_ID = s.Stadium_ID
LEFT JOIN singer_in_concert AS sic
    ON sic.concert_ID = c.concert_ID
WHERE s.Capacity > (
    SELECT AVG(Capacity)
    FROM stadium
)
GROUP BY
    s.Stadium_ID,
    s.Name,
    s.Location,
    s.Capacity,
    s.Highest,
    s.Lowest,
    s.Average
ORDER BY s.Capacity DESC;
```
The query should count only events that actually took place in the stadium.

Use `INNER JOIN` to include only concerts/events that are actually assigned to a stadium, excluding big stadiums with no recorded events:

```sql
SELECT
    s.Stadium_ID,
    s.Name,
    s.Location,
    s.Capacity,
    s.Highest,
    s.Lowest,
    s.Average AS Average_Attendance,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.concert_ID) AS Event_Count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT sic.Singer_ID) AS Singer_Count
FROM stadium AS s
JOIN concert AS c
    ON c.Stadium_ID = s.Stadium_ID
LEFT JOIN singer_in_concert AS sic
    ON sic.concert_ID = c.concert_ID
WHERE s.Capacity > (
    SELECT AVG(Capacity)
    FROM stadium
)
GROUP BY
    s.Stadium_ID,
    s.Name,
    s.Location,
    s.Capacity,
    s.Highest,
    s.Lowest,
    s.Average
ORDER BY s.Capacity DESC;
```
only want to count concerts actually held in the stadium

```sql
SELECT
    s.Stadium_ID,
    s.Name,
    s.Location,
    s.Capacity,
    s.Highest,
    s.Lowest,
    s.Average AS Average_Attendance,
    COUNT(c.concert_ID) AS Concert_Count
FROM stadium AS s
JOIN concert AS c
    ON c.Stadium_ID = s.Stadium_ID
WHERE s.Capacity > (
    SELECT AVG(Capacity)
    FROM stadium
)
GROUP BY
    s.Stadium_ID,
    s.Name,
    s.Location,
    s.Capacity,
    s.Highest,
    s.Lowest,
    s.Average
ORDER BY s.Capacity DESC;
```
I want the query to focus on the stadium with the highest seating capacity.

This focuses only on the stadium/stadiums with the highest seating capacity and counts concerts recorded as held there:

```sql
SELECT
    s.Stadium_ID,
    s.Name,
    s.Location,
    s.Capacity,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.concert_ID) AS Concert_Count
FROM stadium AS s
LEFT JOIN concert AS c
    ON c.Stadium_ID = s.Stadium_ID
WHERE s.Capacity = (
    SELECT MAX(Capacity)
    FROM stadium
)
GROUP BY
    s.Stadium_ID,
    s.Name,
    s.Location,
    s.Capacity;
```
